page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running on Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processors at a constant 3.0 GHz clock rate. Operating on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture without simultaneous multithreading, each core provides single-threaded execution backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of dedicated L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2 GB per core, complemented by 644 GB of attached local solid-state storage.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within median tiers across general multi-threaded computations while showing limitations in single-core tasks. Multi-threaded stress-ng throughput scored 28,883.33 and Geekbench multi-core reached 9,656.0, reflecting linear scaling across the 16 physical cores. Conversely, Geekbench single-core performance registered at 1,092.0 and PassMark encryption scored 2,592.37, trailing contemporary x86 alternatives. Memory bandwidth achieved 119.88 GB/s on uncached 256 MB reads and 68.21 GB/s on writes, delivering stable data flow for Redis SET operations at 20.65 million operations per second and static web throughput of 17.29 GB/s.

The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio provides balanced compute density without the resource overhead of memory-heavy instances, improving infrastructure cost efficiency for compute-centric, cache-friendly tasks. The bundled 644 GB local SSD offers high-speed temporary storage directly to the VM without network disk latency overhead. However, the absence of vector acceleration extensions like AVX-512 and modest single-thread speed limit its viability for heavy single-threaded code or large-scale AI inference, as shown by a 30.85 tokens/sec rate on small LLM text generation.

The D16plds_v5 is suited for ARM-native software compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, containerized microservices, batch processing, and caching tiers like Redis where multi-core scaling and local scratch disk space are prioritized over high memory capacity per core.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute instance built on a 16-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz with dedicated single-threaded cores. Featuring 32 GB of RAM and 644 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage, it delivers a compute-focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates predictable multi-threaded scaling, scoring 28,883.33 in multi-core stress-ng tests and achieving 20.65 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, alongside 17.29 GB/s in static web serving. While single-thread throughput and cryptographic execution lag behind higher-clocked x86 counterparts, its dedicated core architecture eliminates thread contention. The configuration provides strong cost efficiency for scale-out horizontal workloads, making it well suited for ARM-native continuous integration and build pipelines, web services, batch processing, and caching layers requiring fast local scratch disks.
